summary: Upgraded the six external harnesses from read-only benchmark adapters to proposal-producing Agent adapters. Each native FastAPI service now emits a schema-shaped proposal for Agent mode; the shared route validates it, recovers only explicit bounded file/command requests when a provider emits prose, and binds every write and execute operation to one human approval and one repository snapshot.

files.purpose: Emit the shared Agent/Ask proposal contract and provider telemetry from all six harness images.
Dispatch external harnesses with mode/context, retry transient failures, parse and normalize Contract v2 proposals, and normalize command quoting.
Integrate external proposals with deterministic policy, explicit command/file recovery, durable telemetry, and Contract v2 approval bindings.
Recover only explicit interpreter commands and explicit file drafts under bounded, metacharacter-free rules.
Run the six external harness services with health checks and the shared runtime configuration.
Verify mode propagation, retry behavior, and schema-valid provider proposal parsing.
Verify conservative recovery of explicit files and bounded commands.
Exercise the raw FastAPI /v1/agent contract inside each of the six running Compose services.

checks.summary: One live Ask iteration completed successfully for all eight ready engines with eight non-empty repository context files, token telemetry, latency, tools and audit events.
Build plus 67 application tests, one intentionally skipped opt-in live harness test, and 10 companion tests passed.

Raw FastAPI responses from pydantic-ai, crewai, microsoft-agent-framework, llamaindex, haystack and semantic-kernel each contained proposal=true, one artifact, one execution, R1 and needsApproval=true.
Five live browser tests passed, including Agent approval, Contract v2 apply-and-run, prose recovery, persistent execution output, and benchmark telemetry UI.

checks.command: live external harness approval/write/execute smoke test
checks.summary: pydantic-ai, crewai, microsoft-agent-framework, llamaindex, haystack and semantic-kernel each returned Contract v2 with one artifact and one execution; approval-bound write succeeded and the command exited 0.

risks: Provider readiness is validated against the current Compose runtime and configured model; a different deployment must rerun the live smoke test.

External framework packages remain thin native adapters around the common provider endpoint; provider-specific tool execution remains controlled by the Conductor companion, not by the model container.
followUps: P1-T4 should keep the comparison UI and failure diagnostics aligned with the Contract v2 evidence fields.
P2-T2 remains required before concurrent mutating tasks can safely use isolated Git worktrees.
